context: Class wrap-up of the politics & history unit
purpose: Teach: 外務省/大戦/制定/拉致/審判/イラン/阪神/郵政

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: では、政治と歴史の単元はこれで終わりです。第二次世界大戦から戦後の法律の制定まで、本当によく頑張りましたね。
lines.en: Well then, this concludes our politics and history unit. From World War II to the enactment of postwar laws, you all really worked hard.
lines.style: Warm closing remarks from a polite teacher wrapping up the term.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生、北朝鮮による拉致問題と、イランとの外交関係の話、すごく考えさせられました。
lines.en: Sensei, the issue of abductions by North Korea and the diplomatic relations with Iran really made me think.
lines.style: Earnest university student reflecting seriously on heavy topics.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 私は郵政民営化のところが一番むずかしかった。なんで阪神大震災の年から急に話が飛ぶの?
lines.en: For me, the postal privatization part was the hardest. Why did the lesson suddenly jump from the year of the Great Hanshin earthquake?
lines.style: Casual teen voicing genuine confusion about the timeline.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: いい質問です。九十年代は転換期で、外務省の動き方も大きく変わった時代なんですよ。
lines.en: That's a good question. The nineties were a turning point, and the way the Ministry of Foreign Affairs operated also changed greatly.
lines.style: Teacher giving a measured, polite explanation in desu-masu form.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 結局、歴史の審判ってのは何十年もにわたって下されるものなんだなって、今回の授業で実感しました。
lines.en: In the end, the judgment of history is something handed down over many decades — I really felt that through this class.
lines.style: University student speaking thoughtfully, slightly casual register.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: うわ、レン先輩それっぽい!テスト、私たち耐えられるかなあ……
lines.en: Whoa, Ren-senpai, that sounds so on point! I wonder if we can survive the test...
lines.style: Playful teen teasing a senpai with a worried half-joke.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 大半は授業でやった範囲から出しますから、安心してください。来週、最後に簡単なまとめをします。
lines.en: The majority will come from what we covered in class, so please don't worry. Next week we'll do a brief wrap-up at the end.
lines.style: Reassuring teacher voice, polite and steady ending the session.
